entities.summary: Jerónimo de Alderete y Mercado was a Spanish conquistador who played a pivotal role in the early modern era of Spanish colonial expansion in the Americas. Born in Olmedo, Spain in 1518, he was appointed governor of Chile in 1555, but died four months later on April 7, 1556, before he could assume his post. De Alderete's conquests in Chile were part of a broader trend of Spanish colonization that would shape the modern world. His legacy can be seen in the cultural, economic, and political structures that remain in the region to this day. The exact circumstances of his death are not well documented, but it is believed that he died of natural causes or illness in the Chilean town of Santiago.
